name: skeleton
title: Skeleton
description: A placeholder for content on its way: the table's loading cell outside the table, in line, block, value and control shapes; a busy group that names what is loading.
whenToUse: Use it as a placeholder the size of content still loading, so nothing moves when it lands. For a list with nothing in it use Empty; for task progress use Progress.

parts.name: Skeleton
parts.description: A placeholder for content that is on its way. It is the Table's loading cell outside the table: a keyline box on the tint, with a running segment while it waits. ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │░░░░░░▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│ line (k1 soft keyline, tint fill, running segment) └──────────────────────────────┘ - Always aria-hidden. Wrap the loading region in SkeletonGroup, which marks it busy and says what is loading once; a page of skeletons never reads as a list of blanks. - Size it to the real content (lines of the same count, a control of the same frame) so nothing moves when the content lands. - Motion: the segment runs 1100ms linear, the same rhythm as the table. Reduced motion: no segment, the static box alone.

props.name: shape
props.description: line: a run of text; `lines` stacks several, the last one shorter. block: an area (a chart, media, a paragraph you won't line out). value: a number in the count voice. control: the footprint of a control frame (the real control replaces it without moving anything).

props.name: width
props.description: Any CSS length. Defaults: line 100%, value 4ch, control 100%, block 100%.

parts.name: SkeletonGroup
parts.description: The region that is loading. `aria-busy` while `busy`, and one polite status naming what is on its way ("Loading carrier details"); when it lands, the status clears and the content replaces the skeletons in place.

props.name: label
props.description: What is loading, said once while busy ("Loading carrier details").
